_doc: Fields (#122): a wheat field is tilled earth the farmer sows; it ripens into wheat, a sheaf of grain each, and reaped it's tilled earth again. Vines ripen into grapes by themselves, and picked bare grow them again. Coal, iron and gold seams run through the mountains (#42): a mine against one digs it out, and a dug-out seam is worked-out rock. Trees are one trunk each, and a woodcutter plants saplings that grow into trees (#126).

tilled.note: a wheat field laid by a farm and dug by a serf: bare tilled earth, waiting for the farmer to sow it (#122)

wheat_sown.note: a sown wheat field: green shoots, ripe six minutes on

wheat_ripe.note: ripe wheat: the farmer reaps a field's sheaf of grain, and it's tilled earth again, to sow

vines_young.note: a row of vines laid by a vineyard: its grapes ripen six minutes on, by themselves (#122)

vines_ripe.note: ripe grapes on the vine: the winegrower picks them, and they grow again

coal_seam.note: a seam of coal in the mountain: a mine against it digs it out

iron_seam.note: a seam of iron ore in the mountain: a mine against it digs it out

gold_seam.note: a seam of gold ore in the mountain: a mine against it digs it out

worked_out.note: a seam dug out: bare rock

tree.note: a tree in Steading is one trunk: felled in one go and carried home whole (the genre's woodcutter, #126)

sapling.note: a sapling a woodcutter planted: a tree ten minutes on (#126); nothing goes up or through it meanwhile
